title: How To Become A Classroom Management Natural natural/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin dismantles the idea that some teachers are simply born naturals at classroom management, arguing instead that so-called naturals share a specific, learnable set of qualities. He lists eleven traits - being calm, friendly, determined, aware, fun, confident, forgiving, polite, unflappable, dependable, and charismatic - and briefly explains how each one builds influence and rapport with students. He frames charisma as the cumulative result of these individual habits rather than an innate gift, making the point that any teacher can develop it through intention and practice. The article ends with a concrete daily ritual: printing the list, reading it each morning, and mentally rehearsing each quality before students arrive, positioning consistent practice as the real secret behind so-called natural talent.
points: Eleven specific, learnable qualities - calm, friendly, determined, aware, fun, confident, forgiving, polite, unflappable, dependable, charismatic - define a classroom management "natural."
Charisma is presented as the cumulative product of these habits, not an innate trait.
A forgiving, grudge-free daily reset with students builds outsized long-term influence.
A recommended daily practice - reading and meditating on the list each morning - turns the qualities into habit over time.
quotes: If you peek beneath the surface of these “naturals,” if you take a close look at how they interact with students, you’ll discover no mystery at all.

Teachers who radiate a sense of calm have an almost otherworldly effect on students. By their very presence they’re able to settle excitability, erase silliness and immaturity, and focus students on what matters.

Natural teachers have a bit of bulldog in them. An attitude that says: I’m going to teach great lessons, you’re going to be well behaved, and we’re going to have a classroom we love coming to every day.
Teachers with a forgiving nature are afforded greater influence. Every day is a new day in their eyes. No grudges are held.
Charisma is the sum total of the qualities above. For many discouraged teachers, particularly those focused on external rewards and stiffer consequences, it is the missing piece.

Becoming a “natural” in classroom management is like any other goal. It takes desire. It takes purposeful thought. It takes making a choice to pursue what you really want, and then putting your head down and doing it.
